mcq.question: Why does CPU-bound image analysis use processes instead of threads?

options.C: Each process has its own interpreter and GIL, so pure-Python work runs on several cores at once

mcq.explanation: Multiprocessing side-steps the GIL at the cost of start-up and of pickling data between processes.

mcq.question: According to `choose_executor`, when is a process pool *not* worth it for CPU work?

options.A: When there are more than two cores
options.B: When tasks are very small, because start-up and pickling cost more than they save

mcq.explanation: Overhead matters: thousands of tiny tasks run faster in a single process, or when batched with `chunksize`.
